caption: Fourteen months left on the debt review and I finally know where every rand goes. Would you have gone the same route?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R15 800
p/m salary
Living in Aliwal North
slides.body:
Female, 33
Single mother, one daughter (10)
Job: Cleaner, provincial hospital
Net salary: R15 800 p/m

slides.title: Debt review instalment
slides.includes: Medical bill from her hospital stay and a store account, consolidated
slides.body: She was in ICU for four days two years ago. I'm still paying for those four days.

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: Small, but it's five minutes from her school and ten from mine.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers on payday, spaza shop for the rest of the month
slides.body: The spaza is more expensive per item. It's also open when I've got R40 left and nothing else.

slides.title: School fees & uniform
slides.includes: Fees, shoes, the jersey she grew out of in June
slides.body: I work at the hospital that admitted her. I still can't get the fee waiver form right.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi fare, both of us, both directions
slides.body: We take the same taxi most mornings. The driver knows to hoot if we're running late.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, medical aid top-up, phone & data, funeral policy, stokvel
slides.body: The debt review counsellor told me to list these separately. Together they're a third of my salary.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R15 800. Fourteen months left on the debt review. I count them.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon when I started debt review, so I could actually see the instalment against everything else.

No bank login needed.
